question:
Examine and solve the system
$$x+y+z=4$$
$$2x+2y+2z=8$$
$$x-y+z=2$$

(a) Show that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is zero.

(b) Establish that the system is consistent despite the zero determinant.

(c) Determine its complete solution and state the number of solutions.
explanation:
(a)
The coefficient matrix is
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\2 & 2 & 2\\1 & -1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
Since $R_2=2R_1$,
$$|A|=0$$

(b)
The second equation is exactly twice the first equation, including its right-hand side:
$$2(x+y+z)=2(4)=8$$
Thus, the second equation does not produce a contradiction. The first and third equations are independent, so the system is consistent.

(c)
Subtracting the third equation from the first equation,
$$2y=2$$
$$y=1$$
Substituting in the first equation,
$$x+1+z=4$$
$$x+z=3$$
Let $z=t$. Then
$$x=3-t$$
Therefore, the complete solution is
$$x=3-t,\quad y=1,\quad z=t,\quad t\in\mathbb{R}$$
Hence, the system has infinitely many solutions.

options.A:
(a) $|A|=2$
(b) The system is consistent
(c) The unique solution is $(3,1,0)$
options.B:
(a) $|A|=0$
(b) The second equation contradicts the first equation
(c) The system has no solution
options.C:
(a) $|A|=0$ because $R_2=2R_1$
(b) The second equation is exactly twice the first, so the system is consistent
(c) $x=3-t,\ y=1,\ z=t,\ t\in\mathbb{R}$; infinitely many solutions
options.D:
(a) $|A|=0$
(b) The system is consistent
(c) $x=2-t,\ y=2,\ z=t$; infinitely many solutions
